articles.title: Military government in Guinea-Bissau seeks to reshape political system with referendum
articles.author: Nicholas Mwangi
articles.content_excerpt: Guinea-Bissau is set to vote on a new constitution on Sunday, August 30, in a referendum that could alter the country’s political system and strengthen the powers of the presidency. The referendum comes nine months after the military seized control. The crisis traces back to November 23, 2025, when Guinea-Bissau held presidential and parliamentary elections. Both incumbent President Umaro Sissoco Embaló and opposition candidate Fernando Dias da Costa claimed victory. Before the electoral commission could release provisional results, the military intervened on November 26, one day ahead of the announcement suspending the vote count and arresting opposition figures including PAIGC leader Domingos Simões Pereira and PRS’s Francisco da Costa. articles.title: Health activists in India demand affordable breast cancer treatments
articles.author: Ana Vračar
articles.content_excerpt: Health activists and public health experts in India are pushing for affordable breast cancer treatments as the Kerala High Court continues to hear a case originally filed in 2022. The case and the surrounding advocacy concern access to the medications ribociclib and abemaciclib – both of which have demonstrated significant benefits for patients with early-stage breast cancer but remain prohibitively expensive for a large part of the population. Breast cancer represents a true public health crisis in India, noted the Working Group on Access to Medicines and Treatment. In 2024 , of the 780,000 new cancer cases among women, breast cancer accounted for 237,000 diagnoses. Nieto wanted Liam released to his mother, but ICE reportedly refused. The arrest happened just days before Liam was set to start kindergarten. articles.title: Glacier Collapse: 2K Dead or Missing in Nepal-Tibet Flood Is “Glaring Example of Climate Injustice”
articles.content_excerpt: We get a report from Nepal, where at least 547 people are confirmed to have died and over 1,500 are still missing after a glacial collapse on Wednesday sent a wall of ice, mud and rock into a Himalayan river, triggering catastrophic flooding in the Nepal-Tibet border region that swept away entire communities. Nepali authorities say they have rescued more than 3,700 people so far. Geologists say the flash floods were set off by a landslide and glacial avalanche so powerful it set off its own seismic signal. articles.title: “Who Paid, Who Gained”: Juan González on How Chicago Funded Real Estate Instead of Social Services
articles.content_excerpt: A team of researchers led by Democracy Now! ’s Juan González at the University of Illinois Chicago recently released an in-depth study on how, through a program called Tax Increment Financing ( TIF ), Chicago has spent some $16 billion in property taxes it collected over the past 40 years to fund downtown development. The money was supposed to be used to eliminate urban blight. ” TIF funding has actually exacerbated economic inequities throughout the city, pouring more than half of the billions of dollars that it collected into downtown neighborhoods while the 70 other community areas around the city were left to share the other half,” says González. articles.title: “The Lion King” in Quechua?: New Film “Runa Simi” Profiles Indigenous Artist Keeping Language Alive
articles.content_excerpt: Experts estimate that a language is lost every two weeks — and that half of the world’s 7,000 spoken languages could be lost by the end of the century. Quechua is the most widely spoken Indigenous language in the Americas, with approximately 7 to 10 million speakers living primarily in Peru, Bolivia and Ecuador. But like so many Indigenous languages, Qechua is vulnerable due to cultural pressures and discrimination. The new documentary Runa Simi — “our language” in Quechua — follows Fernando Valencia, a Peruvian voice actor, Indigenous activist, radio host and single father, who has dubbed many online clips of animated movies into Quechua from his home in Cusco, Peru. In the film, Fernando pursues his most ambitious goal yet: to fully dub Disney’s animated classic The Lion King into Quechu
